docs.title: Welcome to the Coding Agents for Test Workshop
docs.text:
Thank you for joining the UiPath Coding Agents for Test Workshop!

This Learner's Handbook is your hands-on guide for the workshop. We keep the theory short and get you building fast: in a few hours you'll take a set of requirements all the way to an automated test run, and finish by asking an AI agent for a go/no-go release report in plain English.

Before the workshop

Complete the Prerequisites before the session starts. You install Studio and Delegate, and the hands-on steps depend on them.

Your trainer will share the organization and tenant you'll use during the workshop.

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text:
You'll walk through the full testing lifecycle in UiPath Test Cloud, with AI at every step:

Phase 1 · Set up Orchestrator + TM 1Import the project 2Configure the folder Project, folder, and robot Phase 2 · Plan & test Test Manager 3Evaluate requirements 4Generate test cases 5Run manual tests Autopilot for Testers, plus Delegate for manual runs Phase 3 · Build Studio + Delegate 6Automate test cases Project, Object Repository, automation, test data, and publishing Phase 4 · Run & report TM + Delegate 7Create a test set 8Run and report A regression set → go/no-go PDF

Select a step to jump to it.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this workshop, you will:

✅ Explore agentic features in Test Manager

✅ Delegate at different stages of testing

✅ Agentic and Autopilot for Tester features in Studio

docs.title: How this guide is organized
docs.text:
Section What's inside Prerequisites Accounts, Delegate, and installation Introduction A short tour of Test Cloud, Test Manager, and Coding Agents for Test Hands-On Workshop The eight hands-on steps, from import to the go/no-go report Troubleshooting & Next Steps More prompts to try and fixes for common problems

Next → Prerequisites

Here's something worth holding onto as you work through this workshop

Coding agents don't replace testers — they give testers a new way to work. Instead of clicking through dashboards to find out what failed and why, you ask a question in plain English and get an answer grounded in your real test data.

Robots bring determinism and control, agents bring adaptability and reasoning. This workshop is about putting the two together.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Complete this section before the workshop, then follow the Installation Guide.

docs.title: Accounts and access
docs.text:
Confirm that you can:

✅ Sign in to UiPath Automation Cloud and open the workshop organization and tenant

✅ Open Test Manager and Orchestrator in that tenant

✅ Have an App Testing runtime available for your machine (you'll add it to your folder in 02. Configure the Test Manager Folder)

✅ Use an App Test Developer license, to create Test Automation projects

✅ Create Data Fabric entities, for test data in 06. Automate Test Cases with Studio Desktop and Delegate

✅ Connect UiPath Assistant to your Cloud account

Next → Installation Guide

docs.title: Step 1 — Install UiPath Studio (latest STS)
docs.text:
Install the latest STS version

Delegate is only in Short Term Support (STS) versions of Studio. Install the latest one, even if you already have Studio.

  1. Download and run UiPathStudioCloud.msi.
  2. Launch Studio and sign in to the workshop organization and tenant.
  3. Install the UiPath browser extension: Home → Tools → UiPath Extensions, then select Edge or Chrome.

Check it: Studio shows you signed in to the workshop tenant, and the extension is enabled in your browser.

docs.title: Step 2 — Meet Delegate
docs.text:
UiPath Delegate is UiPath's agent, with the UiPath CLI and skills built in. Describe a task in plain English, and it does it on your machine, in your real browser and apps.

  1. Open UiPath Assistant, and select Delegate in the top ribbon.
  2. Set the work profile: click the chevron next to your user name (bottom left) → Settings → Behavior preferences, and set Work profile to QA / Testing.
  3. Click + New in the left panel to start a new task.

docs.title: Choose how much Delegate does on its own
docs.text:
Set this in Settings → Security → Approval mode:

Approval mode What Delegate does Cautious Asks before every operation Adaptive (recommended) Auto-approves known safe operations, and asks before the rest. Smart approvals also approves what Delegate judges safe Full access Never asks — trusted environments only

Try it:

List the tenant I am connected to.

Delegate acts on your behalf

It uses your UiPath account and permissions, and every action is logged in your name.

Next → Introduction: Test Cloud & Test Manager

docs.title: What is Test Cloud?
docs.text:
Test Cloud is UiPath's cloud platform for application testing. It brings together:

✅ Test Manager — plan, run, manage, and analyze testing

✅ Studio — build and automate test cases

✅ Orchestrator — run test automation at scale

✅ App Test Robot — the robot that runs your automated test cases

✅ Agentic Testing — AI agents, such as Autopilot for Testers and Delegate, at every step

docs.title: What is Test Manager?
docs.text: Test Manager links requirements to test cases, test sets, and results, so you always know what's tested and what's failing.

docs.title: Autopilot for Testers
docs.text:
AI agents built into Test Manager and Studio. Today you'll use:

✅ Evaluate Requirement Quality — checks requirements for clarity, completeness, and testability

✅ Generate Test Cases — generates test cases from requirements

✅ Autopilot for Testers in Studio — turns a manual test case into an automated one, low-code or coded (C#)

docs.title: Delegate for Test
docs.text:
Through the uip tm CLI and the uipath-testcloud skill, Delegate can:

✅ Read test cases, results, and requirement coverage from Test Manager

✅ Write results and test case updates

✅ Trigger test sets and monitor them

That's enough theory — let's build.

Next → 01. Import the Test Manager Project

docs.title: 01. Import the Test Manager Project
docs.text: You start from a ready-made UiBank project: requirements, test cases, test sets, results, and attachments.

docs.title: Download the project file
docs.text:
1. Download Agentic Testing Workshop - Sample Test Manager Project.zip.
  2. Unzip it. You'll import the .tmh file inside.

docs.title: Import it into Test Manager
docs.text:
1. Open Test Manager in the workshop tenant.
  2. On Projects, select import and choose the .tmh file.
  3. Add your name to the Name and Prefix (project key), for example UiBank_AlexS and UIBAS, so your project is unique on the shared tenant.
  4. Start the import. It takes about a minute.

docs.title: Check it with Delegate
docs.text:
Open Delegate and ask, one at a time:

Can you identify the Test Manager project created by me. Provide details.

List the requirements in project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY>, with the test cases linked to each.

Which requirements in project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY> don't have any test cases linked yet?

Pick one test case in project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY> and show me its manual steps and expected results.

✅ Delegate finds your project and answers from your Test Manager data.

Next → 02. Configure the Test Manager Folder

docs.title: 02. Configure the Test Manager Folder
docs.text: To run tests automatically, your project needs an Orchestrator folder with a machine that has an App Testing runtime, linked to the project.

docs.title: Part 1 — Set up your folder and robot
docs.text:
Exercise 1 — Create your folder

  1. Create a personal folder, as your trainer guides you. You'll assign your machine to it.
  2. Enable your user for Personal Automation + Personal workspace, with the Automation Developer role.
  3. In the Enterprise setup, use Custom Windows credentials: your domain\username, no password.
  4. Add your user to your folder.

Exercise 2 — Give your machine an App Testing runtime

  1. Edit your machine template. Under Runtime details, set App Testing to 1, and save.
  2. In your folder, open Machines → Manage Machines in Folder, and add the machine.

docs.title: Part 2 — Link the project to the folder
docs.text:
It's your turn now!

In your Test Manager project, go to Project Settings, open the Automation tab, set Default Folder to the folder you created in Part 1, and click Save.

Skipped this step?

Runs fail with HTTP 400: Please assign folder to project level before executing testcases.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your project has a folder and a robot to run its tests.

Next → 03. Evaluate Requirements

docs.title: 03. Evaluate Requirements
docs.text: Vague or incomplete requirements lead to gaps in testing. The Evaluate Requirement Quality built-in agent checks a requirement for clarity, completeness, and consistency, and suggests fixes.

docs.title: Evaluate it with a built-in agent
docs.text:
1. Open Requirements → Submit Loan Request.
  2. Run the Evaluate Requirement Quality built-in agent on it.

  3. Choose one of the built-in prompts to tell the agent how to evaluate the requirement.

    Editing prompts and adding your own

    The built-in prompts are editable, and you can add custom prompts of your own. Manage them in the Prompt Library, under Project Settings.

  4. In Provide additional context → Add documents, select these project documents (marked P), so the agent checks the requirement against their rules:

    ✅ UiBank Glossary of Terms.txt — undefined banking terms

    ✅ UiBank Security Guidelines.pdf — input validation, data masking, sessions

    ✅ UiBank Accessibility Guidelines.docx — form labels, error messages, keyboard support

    Where do these documents come from?

    They're the project's attachments, under Dashboard → Attachments:

  5. Apply the suggestions you agree with, and update the requirement.

Think about it

Can you spot gaps in the acceptance criteria — an applicant who is exactly 18 or 65, or a loan amount that matches two approval rules? Did the agent find them?

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your requirement is clearer and more testable — ready for generating test cases.

Next → 04. Generate Test Cases

docs.title: 04. Generate Test Cases
docs.text: The Generate Test Cases built-in agent reads a requirement and proposes test cases with manual steps. You review them before they're saved.

docs.title: Generate them with a built-in agent
docs.text:
1. Open the Submit Loan Request requirement.
  2. Run the Generate Test Cases built-in agent on it.

  3. Choose one of the built-in prompts to tell the agent how to generate the test cases.

    Editing prompts and adding your own

    The built-in prompts are editable, and you can add custom prompts of your own. Manage them in the Prompt Library, under Project Settings.

  4. In Provide additional context → Add documents, select:

    ✅ UiBank Regression Tests.xlsx — matches the existing step style, avoids duplicates

    ✅ UiBank Security Guidelines.pdf — adds negative tests

    ✅ UiBank Accessibility Guidelines.docx — adds tests for labels, errors, and keyboard use

    Add documents or Leverage RAG? Add documents Leverage RAG What the agent reads The documents you select, in full Only the relevant passages from a Context Grounding index Best for A few specific documents Large document sets

  5. Optionally, add instructions, for example "Focus on the age and income rules in the acceptance criteria, and apply the security guidelines."

  6. Review the proposals, keep 3 or 4, and create them.

Check it: the requirement shows the new test cases as linked, each with manual steps.

Create one test case that fails

Your trainer guides you to create a test case that's meant to fail. You'll automate it in 06. Automate Test Cases with Studio Desktop and Delegate and add it to the test set in 07. Create a Test Set, so the report in 08. Run and Report has a real failure to show.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
You've gone from a requirement to reviewed, linked test cases in minutes.

Next → 05. Run Manual Tests

docs.title: 05. Run Manual Tests
docs.text:
There are three ways to run a manual test case. Each records its results in Test Manager.

Who runs the steps Apps it can test Setup needed Manual execution assistant You Any None Run autonomously Autopilot, on a robot Web apps A robot in the project's default folder (02. Configure the Test Manager Folder) Delegate Delegate, on your machine Web and desktop apps None

See Executing manual tests.

Manual execution assistant
  1. Go to Test Sets, open a test set, and select Execute → Manually. Allow pop-ups for Test Manager. The manual execution assistant opens in a new window.
  2. Perform each step, then select Set Passed or Set Failed (comment on failures). Set Passed Until Here passes several steps at once.
  3. At any step, capture a screenshot or upload related files as attachments.
  4. Check the postcondition, the state the app must be in after the test. Select Condition Met if it holds.
  5. Select Next, then Done after the last test case.
  6. Check the results in the project's Execution section.

See Executing test sets manually.

Run autonomously

Autonomous Test Execution runs a manual test case with Autopilot, in one click, on a robot.

  1. Go to Test Cases, open a manual test case, and go to the Manual Steps tab. In the right-hand panel, select Run Autonomously.

  2. Confirm the Target Application URL, for example https://uibank.uipath.com. Turn on Live Streaming to watch Autopilot drive the browser, and take over if needed. Leave AI Model as it is.

  3. Select Run.

  4. When it finishes, open the execution: ✅ Logs — each step's result, expected behavior, and screenshots. Expand a step to see what Autopilot did.

    ✅ Execution Log — Autopilot's reasoning, such as how it found an element or compared a result.

See Running Autonomous Test Execution.

No test case yet? Explore the requirement autonomously

Autonomous Exploration is exploratory testing with Autopilot: it learns the app, designs tests, and runs them within a time-box.

  1. Open a requirement → + Autonomous Exploration.
  2. Enter the app URL, set a time-box, and select an AI model. Turn on Live Streaming to watch it explore.
  3. Select Start. When it's Completed, select Show report.

Needs a Windows robot in the project's default folder (set up in 02. Configure the Test Manager Folder), with the UiPath browser extension set to Allow in Incognito. See Running Autonomous Exploration.

docs.title: Run manual tests with Delegate
docs.text:
In this workshop, you'll use Delegate. It runs your test cases, builds new ones, and pushes every result to Test Manager.

Open Delegate.

docs.title: 1 — Run a test case
docs.text:
It's your turn now!

  1. Replace <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> with a test case you created in 04. Generate Test Cases, then paste:

    Run the manual test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY>. Open UiBank at https://uibank.uipath.com, follow the test case's manual steps in the browser, and check every expected result. Take a screenshot at the final validation step and upload it to the test case's assertions. Push the results to Test Manager. If any step failed, explain the reason.

  2. Approve when Delegate asks to push the result.

  3. For any failure, decide: defect in UiBank, or problem with the test case?
Test data already used?

Tests like registering a new user fail if the data was used before. Ask Delegate:

Rerun test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> with new registration data that hasn't been used before, and push the new result to Test Manager.

Check it: Execution → open the new execution → select your test case key. It shows the result, with the screenshot under Assertions.

Think about it

Did Delegate stumble on a step? Autopilot automates these same steps in 06. Automate Test Cases with Studio Desktop and Delegate, so fix them now:

Rewrite the steps of test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> that were unclear during this run, so each one has a single clear action and expected result. Show me the changes before you save them to Test Manager.

docs.title: 2 — Add steps to an empty test case
docs.text:
Your project has a test case, Request Loan, with no steps.

Let's build it with Delegate!

  1. Replace <REQUEST_LOAN_KEY> with its key, then paste:

    Test case <REQUEST_LOAN_KEY> currently has no steps. Add test steps to it based on the linked requirement document and the navigation flow below.

Navigation flow:

Welcome page (https://uibank.uipath.com/welcome)
Open the Products drop-down menu and select Loans.
Expected result: The Loans page opens.

Loans page (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans)
Click the Apply for Loan button.
Expected result: The loan application form is displayed.

Loan application form (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans/apply)
Fill in every required field with the values and rules from the requirement document.
Click Submit.
Expected result: The application is accepted, and the confirmation or result shown matches the acceptance criteria in the requirement.

Instructions:

Take all field names, valid test data, validation rules and expected outcomes from the requirement document. Don't make up any values.
Give each step one action and one expected result.
If the requirement leaves out details a step needs, such as a missing field value or an unclear acceptance criterion, list them as open questions. Don't guess.
Before saving the steps to <REQUEST_LOAN_KEY>, show them to me for review.

  2. Then follow Delegate:

    1. No requirement linked — ask it to link the Submit Loan Request requirement.
    2. Test data — choose the approval path.
    3. Open questions — answer them.
    4. Save the steps — give permission.
    5. Run it — say yes.
    6. Note the loan ID — the approval screen shows it. You'll use it in part 3. Missed it? Ask Delegate: "What loan ID did the approval screen show?"

Check it: Request Loan has manual steps, is linked to the requirement, and has a new result in Execution.

docs.title: 3 — Create a new requirement and test case
docs.text:
The business has documented a new process, Loan lookup, in a Process Design Document (PDD). It isn't in your requirements yet.

It's your turn now!

  1. Download the PDD, Loan lookup process to be tested.docx.

  2. Attach it in Delegate. Replace <YOUR_LOAN_ID> with the loan ID from your Request Loan run in part 2, then paste:

    The attached PDD describes the UiBank loan lookup process. It isn't covered by any requirement in my Test Manager project yet.

1. Create a new requirement for this process.
2. Create a manual test case from the steps and screenshots in the document, and link it to the new requirement.
3. Use loan ID <YOUR_LOAN_ID> as test data.
4. The document ends at Retrieve Loan Details. Add a final step that checks the loan details page shows the same loan ID, along with the rest of the loan's details.

Show me the requirement and the test case before you save them to Test Manager.

  3. Review, give permission to save, and ask Delegate to run it with your loan ID.

Check it: a new Loan lookup requirement, with a linked test case that has manual steps and a result in Execution.

Not quite right? Talk to Delegate

Open the new requirement and test case in Test Manager. Check the title, description, acceptance criteria, steps, and expected results.

Then tell Delegate what to fix, in your own words, just as you'd tell a colleague. For example:

✅ "The test case must check that the loan ID is the same, and that the loan's other details are displayed"

✅ "Don't use the data from the PDD in the test case"

✅ "Add the label 'Delegate' to this test case and requirement"

Keep going until you're happy with both.

Go further — Organize test cases in bulk

  1. Add a label to your test cases:

    Add the label "Delegate" to every test case you created or ran in this session.

  2. Create a Test Tier custom field and set it on the labeled test cases:

    Create a custom field definition for test cases in project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY>:
- Name: Test Tier
- Description: How often this test should run: every build, daily, or before release.
- Object type: Test Cases
- Data type: Label
- Possible values: Smoke, Core, Extended

Then, for every test case with the label "Delegate", set Test Tier to "Smoke".

Check it: open a labeled test case. Its Details tab shows Test Tier: Smoke.

Beyond running tests — Delegate across the whole manual testing cycle

Ideas to try on your own project, in your own words:

✅ Find test ideas — from a requirement's acceptance criteria, or from a screenshot of a screen, including boundary and negative cases.

✅ Write the steps — turn those ideas into manual test cases and link them to the requirement.

✅ Run them with you — Delegate runs the steps and stops to ask when it needs input you have, such as login details.

✅ Record the results — create test results with screenshots of failed steps, and upload them to Test Manager.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your test cases are proven against the real application, with results in Test Manager. Next, you'll connect Studio to automate them.

Next → 06. Automate Test Cases with Studio Desktop and Delegate

docs.title: 06. Automate Test Cases with Studio Desktop and Delegate
docs.text:
Automate your manual test cases in Studio with Delegate. Each automation stays linked to its test case in Test Manager.

Access required

You need an App Test Developer license to create and publish Test Automation projects.

docs.title: What you'll do
docs.text:
You switch between two tools on this page. Each step is labelled with the one it uses:

Tool What you do Delegate Paste the prompt in Delegate, then wait and watch it build in Studio Studio Desktop Work in Studio Desktop yourself, with Autopilot for Testers

Click a step to jump to it.

Delegate Create a Test Automation project Install the UI Automation package Link Studio to your Test Manager project Build the Object Repository Studio Desktop Automate the test cases Generate test data Delegate Publish the test cases

docs.title: Create a Test Automation project
docs.text:
Delegate

Create a Studio Test Automation project named UiBank Tests.

Check it: UiBank Tests opens in Studio, in Documents\UiPath\UiBank Tests.

docs.title: Install the UI Automation package
docs.text:
Delegate

Install the latest stable UI Automation activities package in UiBank Tests.

Check it: Manage Packages → Project Dependencies lists UiPath.UIAutomation.Activities.

docs.title: Link Studio to your Test Manager project
docs.text:
Delegate

Replace <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY> with your project key, then paste:

Connect this project to my Test Manager project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY>, then open Test Explorer to show its test cases.

Check it: the connection icon is green, and Test Explorer lists your test cases.

docs.title: Build the Object Repository
docs.text:
Delegate

The Object Repository stores the app's screens and UI elements for every test case to reuse.

Building it by hand is usually one of the slowest parts of test automation: you capture every screen and element yourself. Tell Delegate what to capture, and it builds the repository for you. To cover every screen and element the test cases need, use the prompt below.

Continue in Delegate

  1. Paste:

    Create an Object Repository in UiPath Studio Desktop for the UiBank web app running in Chrome.

Application
- Name: UiBankORForChrome
- Browser: Chrome
- Capture each element live in the browser
- Prefer stable selectors (id, name, aria-label, visible text) over index-based ones
- Avoid dynamic values in selectors
- Name each element exactly as listed below

Screens and elements

1. Screen: Welcome (https://uibank.uipath.com/welcome)
   - Username (input)
   - Password (input)
   - Sign In (button)
   - Products (dropdown menu)
   - Loans (menu item in the Products dropdown; open Products first so Loans is visible when you capture it)

2. Screen: Loans (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans)
   - Apply For Loan (button)
   - Already Have A Loan (button)

3. Screen: Loan Application (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans/apply)
   - Email Address of Requester (input)
   - Loan Amount Requested (input)
   - Loan Term (dropdown)
   - Current Yearly Income Before Taxes (input)
   - Age (input)
   - Submit Loan Application (button)

4. Screen: Loan Result (the results view shown after you submit the loan application)
   - Result Text: the full text block of the response
   - Rate: only the number shown below "With a fantastic rate of:", without the "%" sign
   - Loan ID: the value shown below "Your new loan ID is:"
   Anchor these elements to their label text, not to the changing values, so the selectors work for any result.
   To reach this screen, submit the form with sample valid values. Save the Loan ID for screen 6.

5. Screen: Loan Lookup (https://uibank.uipath.com/loans/lookup)
   - Loan ID (input)
   - Retrieve Loan Details (button)

6. Screen: Loan Lookup Result (the results view shown after you look up a Loan ID)
   - Result Text: the full text block of the response
   - Loan ID: the value shown beside its label, anchored to the label text
   To reach this screen, look up the Loan ID you saved from screen 4.

Acceptance criteria
- All 6 screens and 20 elements exist under UiBankORForChrome, named as above
- Every selector validates (highlights the correct element) on its live screen
- Report any element you could not capture reliably, and why

  2. Don't use your desktop or browser while it captures.

Write your own Object Repository prompt

Describe what you need in plain language, such as the app, its screens, and the elements to capture. Delegate can also review and fine-tune your prompt, or fix it when something's missed.

Check it:

  1. In Studio's Object Repository panel, expand UiBankORForChrome. It lists all 6 screens and their elements. If it's empty, reload the project.

  2. Open UiBank in Chrome on the Welcome screen. Right-click an element, such as Username, and select Highlight.

  3. In the browser, the element is outlined in green, and its label anchor in blue. Repeat for a few elements on each screen.

If an element doesn't highlight, ask Delegate to recapture it.

Complete this step before you continue

Autopilot for Testers builds your test cases from the Object Repository elements. Without them, it can't automate the test cases in the next step.

Switch to Studio Desktop

Delegate has set up the project and built the Object Repository. For the next two steps, you work directly in Studio Desktop, using Autopilot for Testers to turn your manual test cases into automations.

docs.title: Automate the test cases with Studio Desktop
docs.text:
Studio Desktop

It's your turn now!

  1. In Test Explorer, right-click a manual test case → Generate Test Case with Autopilot.
  2. Check it uses Object Repository elements and the expected results. If not, ask Delegate to fix it.

  3. Check the Use Application/Browser cards. The data-driven test in the next section must open and close the app once per row, and your requirement and test case may not say so.

    ✅ First card: set Open to Always.

    ✅ Last card: set Close to Always.

    ✅ Cards in between: keep Open and Close as Never.

  4. Run it locally.

Check it: at least 2 automated test cases pass locally, and the test case meant to fail, from 04. Generate Test Cases, fails.

Optional: Fix the activity display names

Autopilot names each activity after its manual step, including the test data, which makes long, hard-to-read display names.

  1. Replace Submit Short-Term Request with the name of the test case you generated, then paste in Delegate:

    I've created test case Submit Short-Term Request using autopilot feature in Studio. Fix the Display names. Provide appropriate names.

  2. Reload the test case in Studio and check the new names.

docs.title: Generate test data
docs.text:
Studio Desktop

TBD

docs.title: Publish the test cases
docs.text:
Delegate

Switch back to Delegate

Your test cases are automated. Go back to Delegate to publish them.

Paste:

Set the <YOUR_TEST_CASE_NAMES> test cases in UiBank Tests as publishable and publish the project.

Check it: in Orchestrator, each automated test case shows in Test Cases.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your test cases are automated, data-driven, and published, ready to run from Test Manager.

Next → 07. Create a Test Set

docs.title: 07. Create a Test Set
docs.text: A test set groups test cases that run together.

docs.title: Create it
docs.text:
It's your turn now!

  1. In Test Manager, go to Test Sets → Create Test Set.
  2. Name it Regression Test Set, and click Create.

  3. Open the test set → Tasks → Assign Test Cases. Choose one, then select Assign:

    ✅ Static Assignment — pick your automated test cases, including the one meant to fail. The set always runs exactly these.

    ✅ Dynamic Assignment — enter labels. Each time the set runs, it includes every test case with at least one of them. Use a label only your automated test cases have.

See Assigning test cases to test sets.

Check it: Regression Test Set lists your automated test cases, including the one meant to fail.

Do a test run (optional)

Open the test set → Execute → Automated, then check Execution. Every test case should have a result. A real failure is fine — that's what the report is for.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Everything is in place to run and report.

Next → 08. Run and Report

docs.title: 08. Run and Report
docs.text:
It's release night, and the release manager wants to know: can we ship? Ask Delegate to run the test set and write the go/no-go report — in one prompt.

Check these first

✅ Your robot is available — connected and not busy, in your Orchestrator folder.

✅ You know your project key, and Regression Test Set from 07. Create a Test Set has your automated test cases.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
It's your turn now!

  1. Open Delegate.

  2. Replace <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY>, then paste:

    Trigger the Regression Test Set of project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY> in Test Manager and wait for it to finish. Once finished, create a release manager report in PDF for that test set, and save it in Documents\UiPath\Reports. I need a go/no-go summary before tonight's sign-off meeting. Highlight the failures blocking the release.

  3. Approve the run when Delegate asks. It's the only action that changes anything — a real execution on your robot.

  4. Wait a few minutes while it runs the set, fetches the results, counts them, and finds the top failing test cases.
  5. If Delegate asks where to save the report, select Other folder path and enter Documents\UiPath\Reports, then select Next. Keep the default file name, and select Submit.
Run a single test case instead 
Run test case <YOUR_TEST_CASE_KEY> in project <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY> in Test Manager, wait for it to finish, and tell me whether it passed. If it failed, explain why.

docs.title: Check the report
docs.text:
Delegate gives the path to the saved report and summarizes the key numbers in the chat. Compare them with Execution in Test Manager. The report shows:

✅ Scope — the executions it covers

✅ Totals — passed, failed, none, and restricted

✅ Success rate

✅ Top failing test cases

✅ Recommendation — GO or NO-GO, and why

Saved as .md instead of PDF?

Ask Delegate:

Create a PDF of the report and copy to my Downloads folder

Think about it

Does the recommendation match what you'd decide? What else would a release manager want to see? How long would this report take you to build by hand?

docs.title: Schedule it as a routine
docs.text:
A report you run once is useful. One that arrives every morning is better. You don't need to set this up today, but here's how it works.

Save it as a routine. Once Delegate has run a task, you can ask it to save the task as a reusable routine. For example: "Save this run-and-report task as a routine called <YOUR_PROJECT_KEY> Release Report." The routine appears under Routines in Delegate's left panel, ready to run again on demand.

Put it on a schedule. Under Scheduled routines, a Day / Week / Month calendar shows every routine with a time slot. New routines wait in the Not scheduled list below it. Drop one onto a time slot or set it to recur, for example weekdays at 8:00 AM.

The machine must be on

A scheduled routine runs only if the machine it runs on is powered on and signed in at the scheduled time.

docs.text:

✅ "Summarize the failures in three bullet points I can paste into Slack."

docs.title: Delegate
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix Delegate isn't in UiPath Assistant's top ribbon Your Studio version may be too old. Install the latest STS version from the Installation Guide, and ask your trainer to confirm your access. Delegate asks for approval on every step The approval mode is Cautious. In Settings → Security, switch it to Adaptive. Delegate can't find your project Delegate is signed in to the wrong tenant. Sign in again with the organization and tenant from your trainer, then click + New to start a new task.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause / fix HTTP 400: Please assign folder to project level before executing testcases. The project has no default folder. Complete 02. Configure the Test Manager Folder, Part 2. Test cases are skipped with no result They're manual — not linked to a published automation. Complete Publish the test cases and check each test case shows an automation. The run stays pending or hangs The robot is busy or disconnected. In Orchestrator, check the machine in your folder is connected and has an App Testing runtime. Tests fail with "Cannot communicate with the browser" A robot-side problem with the UiPath browser extension, not a product defect. Check the extension is installed and enabled on the robot machine.

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause / fix You can't find the report Delegate shows the path when it finishes. If you chose Current working directory, the file is inside the Assistant install folder, which is hard to find. Ask Delegate "Create a PDF of the report and copy to my Downloads folder". The report numbers don't match Test Manager Make sure you're comparing the same execution. Ask Delegate which execution ID it used.
